intendedAction: Record orientation for deciding that the MCP bridge server refactor should be an observed open-weight model workload rather than manual pre-observation maintenance.
notes: User clarified that the MCP server refactor should be done by open-weight models and observed so ForgePilot can gather data.

This changes the sequence: the MCP refactor is not silent operator maintenance before observation; it becomes one of the first real observed workloads after the guarded runner path is proven safe enough.
Manual GPT/operator work should prepare packet constraints, success criteria, forbidden changes, test commands, audit checklist, and comparison criteria.
Open-weight models should perform the implementation, with ForgePilot recording verification, audit, comparison, and admission evidence.

No approval, clearance creation, approval consumption, disable-switch change, runner start contact, OpenCode start, prompt submission, wait call, or canary execution is in scope for this decision packet.
observationSemantics: operator workflow trace is control-plane evidence, not model-performance evidence
